items.pronunciation_notes: The dot over क is an m before the प: kam-pa-nii.

learn.title_en: A borrowed word that landed on a predictable ending
learn.explanation_en: कंपनी comes from English and is feminine — but unlike बस and मीटिंग, this one you could have guessed, because it ends in -ी. Borrowed nouns take their gender arbitrarily, and when the borrowed shape happens to match a Hindi pattern the gender usually follows that pattern. It declines like नौकरी: कंपनी में in the singular, कंपनियों में in the plural.

examples.hindi: मैं एक कंपनी में काम करता हूँ
examples.read_as: maiṁ ek kampanii meṁ kaam kartaa huuṁ
examples.note: में for being inside an organisation, and कंपनी is oblique before it.
बड़ी is feminine, agreeing with कंपनी.
The Class 4 oblique plural, exactly like नौकरियों.

common_error.why_en: कंपनी ends in -ी and is feminine, so a marked adjective takes -ी too.

practice.question: कंपनी
practice.explanation_en: कंपनी is a company, feminine, and it declines like नौकरी.

game.question_en: Which postposition goes with कंपनी when you work there?
game.explanation_en: कंपनी में काम करना — में for being inside an organisation.

tts_strings: मैं एक कंपनी में काम करता हूँ

items.pronunciation_notes: Starts with the independent vowel ई, held long: ii-mel.

learn.title_en: ईमेल takes भेजना, and करना also works
learn.explanation_en: ईमेल is masculine and Class 2, so it never changes. Its main verb is भेजना, to send: ईमेल भेजो. But ईमेल करना is equally common in speech, because करना attaches to almost any borrowed noun to make a verb out of it — ईमेल करना, फ़ोन करना, मैसेज करना. That is a productive pattern worth knowing: when a new English word arrives, करना is how Hindi turns it into an action.

examples.note: The तुम imperative — भेजना is transitive.
करना attached to a borrowed noun, which is the general pattern.
आना is intransitive, so the perfective is available.

common_error.why_en: लेना is to take. An email is sent or made, not taken, whatever direction it is travelling.

practice.question: ईमेल
practice.explanation_en: ईमेल is an email, masculine, and unchanged in the plural.

game.explanation_en: ईमेल भेजना. ईमेल करना is equally common, since करना verbs almost any borrowed noun.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dotted ज़ buzzes and the म is doubled: zim-me-daa-rii, four syllables.

learn.title_en: ज़िम्मेदारी — the -ी that makes abstract nouns
learn.explanation_en: ज़िम्मेदारी is responsibility, feminine and predictable from its -ी. It is built from ज़िम्मेदार, responsible, with the same -ी suffix that turned ख़ुश into ख़ुशी and कमज़ोर into कमज़ोरी. That suffix is one of the most productive things in Hindi vocabulary: adjective plus -ी gives you the abstract noun, and the result is always feminine. Once you notice it, a lot of long words stop being intimidating.

examples.note: मेरी is feminine, agreeing with ज़िम्मेदारी.
The तुम imperative — लेना is transitive.
The adjective, which is unmarked and never changes.

common_error.why_en: Every noun formed with the -ी suffix is feminine, without exception. That makes the gender predictable here.

practice.question: ज़िम्मेदारी
practice.explanation_en: ज़िम्मेदारी is responsibility, formed from the adjective ज़िम्मेदार with -ी.

game.explanation_en: ज़िम्मेदारी लेना — responsibility is taken, exactly as in English.

summary.recap_en: करना attaches to almost any borrowed noun to make a verb — ईमेल करना, फ़ोन करना — which is how Hindi absorbs new vocabulary. And adjective plus -ी gives an abstract noun that is always feminine: ख़ुशी, कमज़ोरी, ज़िम्मेदारी.
summary.next_up_en: Next: problems, being ready, and what counts as necessary — closing the work block.

items.pronunciation_notes: The स्य is a single cluster with no vowel between: sa-mas-yaa.

collocation.english: for there to be a problem

learn.title_en: The fifth feminine noun ending in -ा
learn.explanation_en: समस्या is a problem, and it joins चिंता, हवा, यात्रा and दवा as a feminine noun ending in -ा. Five of them now, and four of the five come from Sanskrit — which is a genuine hint, though not a rule you can rely on. The plural is समस्याएँ, formed with -एँ as every feminine -ा noun does, never समस्ये. The common phrase is कोई समस्या नहीं, no problem, which you will hear constantly.

examples.note: A set phrase, and the standard reassurance.
बड़ी is feminine, which proves समस्या is.
The plural takes -एँ, like चिंताएँ and दवाएँ.

common_error.why_en: The -ा ending misleads again. समस्या is feminine, like the four before it.

practice.question: समस्या
practice.explanation_en: समस्या is a problem, and it is feminine despite the -ा ending.

game.explanation_en: समस्या होना — a problem exists rather than being done.

items.pronunciation_notes: The first syllable holds a diphthong close to the vowel in English 'tie': tai-yaar.

learn.title_en: तैयार covers ready, prepared and willing
learn.explanation_en: तैयार is unmarked, so it never changes, and it stretches further than English ready. तैयार हो? means are you ready, खाना तैयार है means the food is ready, and मैं तैयार हूँ can also mean I am willing. With करना it becomes transitive — खाना तैयार करना, to prepare food — so the same word covers both being ready and making something ready, and the verb tells you which.

examples.note: The adjective is identical whoever is speaking.
A masculine subject, and still तैयार.
An instruction, using होना rather than करना because you are readying yourself.

common_error.why_en: तैयारी is the noun preparation. The adjective is तैयार, and the -ी makes it a different word.

practice.question: तैयार
practice.explanation_en: तैयार is ready or prepared, and it never changes its form.

game.question_en: Which verb goes with तैयार when you get yourself ready?
game.explanation_en: तैयार होना for readying yourself. तैयार करना means preparing something else.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dotted ज़ buzzes and the middle vowel is long: za-ruu-rii.

learn.title_en: Another -ी adjective that does not change
learn.explanation_en: ज़रूरी ends in -ी and is unmarked, exactly like दुखी back in level one. It is worth seeing the pair together, because after Module 6 a final -ी reads as feminine agreement and it is not. यह ज़रूरी है for a masculine subject, यह बात ज़रूरी है for a feminine one, and the word is identical. The related noun is ज़रूरत, need, which is feminine and takes होना: मुझे ज़रूरत है, I need it.

examples.note: The adjective with a masculine subject.
बात is feminine and the adjective is unchanged.
The noun ज़रूरत, feminine, with the person marked by को.

common_error.why_en: There is no ज़रूरा. Working backwards from the -ी to invent a masculine form is the same trap दुखी sets.

practice.question: ज़रूरी
practice.explanation_en: ज़रूरी is necessary or important, and it is unmarked despite ending in -ी.

game.explanation_en: ज़रूरी होना. The related noun ज़रूरत also takes होना, with the person marked by को.

summary.recap_en: The work block is complete at fifteen words. समस्या is the fifth feminine noun in this module ending in -ा, and ज़रूरी is the second unmarked adjective ending in -ी — two endings that look like they should tell you something and do not.
summary.next_up_en: Next: school and study, including one collocation that runs exactly opposite to English.

items.pronunciation_notes: The ढ़ is a breathy flap and the word ends on two vowels running together: pa-ṛhaa-ii.

learn.title_en: The -आई ending, and why it is always feminine
learn.explanation_en: पढ़ाई is studying, formed from पढ़ना with the suffix -आई. That suffix turns a verb into the noun for the activity, and everything it makes is feminine: पढ़ाई from पढ़ना, लिखाई from लिखना, कमाई from कमाना. So a word ending in -आई is as reliably feminine as one ending in -ी, which makes this a second predictable pattern rather than another thing to memorise. पढ़ाई करना is to study, alongside the plain verb पढ़ना.

examples.note: करता agrees with the subject, not with पढ़ाई.
Both अच्छी and रही are feminine, agreeing with पढ़ाई.
The plain verb पढ़ना, for the act rather than the activity.

common_error.why_en: Words ending in -आई are always feminine, so everything agreeing with पढ़ाई takes -ी.

practice.question: पढ़ाई
practice.explanation_en: पढ़ाई is studying as an activity, formed from पढ़ना with -आई.

game.explanation_en: पढ़ाई करना — to study. The activity noun takes करना.

items.pronunciation_notes: The क्ष is a single cluster, close to ksh: pa-riik-shaa.

learn.title_en: The student gives the exam and the teacher takes it
learn.explanation_en: This is the collocation that runs backwards from English. परीक्षा देना means to sit an exam — the student gives it. परीक्षा लेना means to set and administer one — the teacher takes it. English has it the other way round entirely, so a learner translating directly says exactly the wrong thing and claims to be running the examination. Learn the pair together. परीक्षा is also the sixth feminine noun in this module ending in -ा.

examples.note: देना for the student, and the future because देना is transitive.
लेना for the examiner, with respectful plural agreement.
The noun standing alone with होना.

common_error.why_en: लेना would mean you are the one setting the paper. The candidate gives the exam in Hindi.

practice.question: परीक्षा
practice.explanation_en: परीक्षा is an exam, and it is feminine despite ending in -ा.

game.question_en: Which verb goes with परीक्षा when you are the student?
game.explanation_en: परीक्षा देना — the student gives the exam. लेना belongs to the examiner.

items.pronunciation_notes: The stress falls on the long second syllable: sa-vaal.

learn.title_en: सवाल पूछना, and who you ask takes से
learn.explanation_en: सवाल is a question, masculine and Class 2. The verb is पूछना, to ask, and the person you ask takes से rather than को: मुझसे सवाल मत पूछो, do not ask me questions. That से catches people out because English uses no preposition at all there. सवाल also means a problem in the mathematical sense — a sum to solve — so सवाल हल करना is to solve a problem.

examples.note: The तुम imperative — पूछना is transitive.
मुझसे is मैं fused with से, and मत negates the imperative.
मुश्किल is unmarked and never changes.

common_error.why_en: पूछना takes से for the person asked, not को. The same से appears with प्यार करना.

practice.question: सवाल
practice.explanation_en: सवाल is a question, masculine, and also a sum to be solved.

game.question_en: Which postposition marks the person you ask?
game.explanation_en: मुझसे सवाल पूछो — पूछना takes से for the person asked.

summary.recap_en: Words ending in -आई are reliably feminine, which makes पढ़ाई predictable. परीक्षा is not — and its collocation runs backwards from English, with the student giving the exam and the examiner taking it.
summary.next_up_en: Next: answers, mistakes and the teacher, and the postpositions each of them takes.

items.pronunciation_notes: Long aa in the second syllable and a soft final b: ja-vaab.

learn.title_en: सवाल and जवाब, question and answer
learn.explanation_en: जवाब is an answer, masculine and Class 2, and it pairs with सवाल so tightly that सवाल-जवाब together means a question-and-answer session or an interrogation. The verb is देना, and the person you answer takes को: मुझे जवाब दो, answer me. So the pair takes different postpositions — you ask a person से and answer them को — which is worth noticing because English marks neither.

examples.note: The तुम imperative of देना.
The person answered takes को, unlike with पूछना.
सही is unmarked and means correct.

common_error.why_en: देना takes को for the recipient. से belongs with पूछना, and the two are easy to swap.

practice.question: जवाब
practice.explanation_en: जवाब is an answer, masculine, and it pairs with सवाल.

game.explanation_en: जवाब देना — an answer is given, and the person answered takes को.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dotted ग़ is made further back than a plain ग: gal-tii.

learn.title_en: ग़लती करना, and ग़लत for the thing itself
learn.explanation_en: ग़लती is a mistake, feminine and predictable from its -ी. The verb is करना — you do a mistake in Hindi rather than making one — and the adjective ग़लत means wrong or incorrect. So जवाब ग़लत है is the answer is wrong. There is also a second way to say you made one: मुझसे ग़लती हुई, using होना and से, which carefully avoids blaming anyone and is noticeably gentler. It is also the version available to you now, since it needs no ने.

examples.note: The negative imperative with मत, and करना is safe outside the perfective.
होना is intransitive, so this version is available to you now.
ग़लत is the unmarked adjective, and it never changes.

common_error.why_en: ग़लती is the noun mistake. To describe something as wrong you need the adjective ग़लत.

practice.question: ग़लती
practice.explanation_en: ग़लती is a mistake, feminine, and ग़लत is the adjective wrong.

game.explanation_en: ग़लती करना — you do a mistake in Hindi. मुझसे ग़लती हुई is the gentler alternative.

items.pronunciation_notes: Retroflex ट as with every English loanword: ṭii-char.

learn.title_en: टीचर takes plural agreement out of respect
learn.explanation_en: टीचर is borrowed from English and used far more in speech than the Hindi अध्यापक or शिक्षक, which belong to writing. The thing to notice is the agreement: teachers, like doctors and elders, usually take plural verbs as a mark of respect. टीचर आ रहे हैं for a single teacher, not आ रहा है. That is the same grammatical plural that makes आप polite, applied to a third person, and using the singular can sound dismissive.

examples.note: Plural agreement for one person, out of respect.
पूछना takes से for the person asked.
अच्छी is feminine for a woman, and हैं is still the respectful plural.

common_error.why_en: Not ungrammatical, but singular agreement for a teacher sounds curt. Respect is expressed through the plural.

practice.question: टीचर
practice.explanation_en: टीचर is a teacher, and the word is used for both men and women.

game.question_en: Which postposition goes with टीचर when you ask them something?
game.explanation_en: टीचर से पूछना — पूछना always takes से for the person asked.

summary.recap_en: पूछना takes से and देना takes को, so you ask a person से and answer them को — a distinction English does not mark at all. Teachers and doctors take plural agreement as a mark of respect, which is the same grammatical plural that makes आप polite.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the classroom, understanding, and a conversation before an exam.

items.pronunciation_notes: The क्ल is a single cluster with no vowel between: klaas.

collocation.english: to take or teach a class

learn.title_en: क्लास लेना means teaching it, not attending it
learn.explanation_en: क्लास is borrowed from English and is feminine — another gender assigned on arrival with no rule behind it. Its collocation carries the same reversal as परीक्षा: क्लास लेना is what the teacher does, taking the class, while a student attends with क्लास में जाना or क्लास अटेंड करना. The Hindi word कक्षा exists and means the same thing in more formal contexts, including a school year group.

examples.note: लेना for the teacher, with respectful plural agreement.
क्लास is oblique before में, though nothing visible changes.
हुई is feminine, which proves क्लास is.

common_error.why_en: क्लास लेना means you are teaching it. A student goes to class rather than taking it.

practice.question: क्लास
practice.explanation_en: क्लास is a class or lesson, and Hindi treats it as feminine.

game.question_en: Which verb goes with क्लास when the teacher runs it?
game.explanation_en: क्लास लेना — the teacher takes the class. A student goes to it instead.

items.pronunciation_notes: The middle vowel almost vanishes and the झ is breathy: sa-majh-naa.

learn.title_en: Two ways to say you understand, and one is easier
learn.explanation_en: समझना is to understand, and it is transitive — मैं समझता हूँ, I understand. But Hindi also has समझ आना, where understanding comes to you: मुझे समझ आता है. The second is worth having now for a practical reason. समझना is transitive, so its perfective needs ने and is not yet available, while समझ आना is intransitive and works in every tense. मुझे समझ आया, I understood, is a sentence you can build today.

examples.note: The habitual present, which is safe with a transitive verb.
आना is intransitive, so the perfective is available now.
The auxiliary is dropped after नहीं, as usual in the habitual.

common_error.why_en: समझना is transitive, so its perfective needs ने. The समझ आना version avoids the problem entirely.

practice.question: समझना
practice.explanation_en: समझना is to understand, and समझाना is to explain.

game.question_en: Which verb pairs with समझ so you can use the past right now?
game.explanation_en: समझ आना is intransitive, so मुझे समझ आया works without ने.

items.pronunciation_notes: The question falls away at the end, with कब है unstressed.

learn.title_en: Four lines, and the last one avoids ने
learn.explanation_en: The first line hangs on gender again — परीक्षा is feminine, so तुम्हारी rather than तुम्हारा. The last line is worth noticing for a different reason: मुझे यह सवाल समझ नहीं आता uses समझ आना rather than समझना, which means it needs no ने and works in any tense. A learner who reached for समझना here would be stuck, because its perfective is still two modules away. Choosing the intransitive partner is often the way around that.

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: हाँ, लेकिन मुझे यह सवाल समझ नहीं आता।
lines.read_as: haaṁ, lekin mujhe yah savaal samajh nahiiṁ aataa.
lines.english: Yes, but I do not understand this question.

common_error.why_en: परीक्षा is feminine despite the -ा ending, so the possessive is तुम्हारी.

practice.question: मुझे समझ नहीं आता
practice.explanation_en: Literally understanding does not come to me — the intransitive way of saying it.

game.question_en: Listen to the first line. Which word is missing?
game.explanation_en: परीक्षा is feminine, so the possessive is तुम्हारी.

tts_strings: हाँ, लेकिन मुझे यह सवाल समझ नहीं आता।

summary.recap_en: क्लास लेना and परीक्षा लेना both belong to the teacher, not the student — the same reversal twice. समझ आना is the intransitive partner of समझना, and choosing it lets you use the past tense two modules early.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the last of the school block, then shopping and money.
